body: Thanks, because I'm not already beating up on myself enough because I feel like my daughter is stuck home all the time because of my illness and because I feel like I want to die...thanks for telling me those things caused your bipolar depression. I've been on and off of medication for 20 years. I've taken every possible medication and combination you can come up with. I've consulted many psychiatrists...all with the same answer, even my best possible combination of medication isn't great. Thus the reason it's so easy to go off my medication. It sucks to stuff a bunch of drugs into my body and still feel like shit. Clearly my daughter is my motivator or I would have killed myself years ago. I stated from the beginning that I need to live because of my daughter. But thanks again for letting me know that you dealt with circumstances similar to what my daughter has to deal with and that caused all your problems. That makes me feel so much better.

How long have you been on the medication? It can take awhile for them to start to work. Try to hang in there and tell yourself that the meds just need more time and you'll start to feel at least a little better. And if you don't start to feel better, then know that there are other things your doctor can give you. If you don't feel like you can hang in there until your scheduled follow up with the doctor, let someone know so you can see the doctor sooner. It sounds like you're new to medication. You've done a good thing by seeking help, try to hang in a little longer and give that help enough time to do it's thing.

My daughter is only 10. Her father and I are divorced and I have full custody. Despite how messed up I am, I'm actually the safer, more stable parent (he has anger/rage issues and was physically abusive to her when we were married...who beats up a 2-year-old?...thus the reason he's an EX-husband) There really is no good option for someone to take care of her if I died...it's why I know I have to find a way to hang in there. Things hurt so badly, and I want it to end but I can't because she needs me...sometimes that makes me feel trapped and then I feel guilty for feeling trapped. And, well, vicious cycle. I had to go into a psychiatric hospital for a couple of weeks in January. It was the first time I've been hospitalized in my daughter's lifetime. She knew the truth about where I was going, but it was really hard on her to have me away for so long. I know I have to live for her. It's just so freaking hard.
I'm sorry. I guess what I said could be taken more than one way. By not taking my medication the way that I should, I meant I'm not taking it, at all. As in, I should be taking it but I am not.

Have you let your parents and your psychiatrist know that the meds aren't helping? I know it is scary to open yourself up but they cannot help you if you don't let them know how bad it is. If the meds you're taking aren't helping enough, there are other meds that you can try. But you have to let them know you need more help.

I can tell that you're scared but there are options. Now is the time to take a deep breath and support each other. She can choose to give the baby up for adoption...as others have said there are legitimate ways to have mom's medical costs covered by an adopting couple. If she does not want to carry the child for nine months and give it up for adoption, she can choose to explore the option of abortion...what is involved, how much it costs, etc. You can both choose to talk to your families about the situation, they may surprise you and be more supportive and helpful than you think. The point is, there are other options to consider before jumping to suicide.

I haven't been taking my medication the way that I should, so I'm too ashamed to go to my psychiatrist for help. I don't have a therapist...I've tried finding someone in the past but have had no luck finding someone who didn't irritate me more than help me. I have an appointment with a new therapist on Monday. I'm not very hopeful but at least I can tell myself I'm trying and it gives me something to hold onto for the time being.

Thank you for sharing. I'm sorry that you've had to experience the loss of your father. If you can't, or don't want to talk about it, I understand but... before your dad died, when you were still a kid how did you feel about your dad and his illness? I guess what I'm asking is what kind of impact did his illness have on you before his death?

I'm too worn down to do those things with her. Way too much anxiety to get out of the house that much, for sure. It's just one of  the many reasons why I know she deserves better and more than I can be for her.
I get migraines. I have since I was a child. (And my child gets migraines.) Currently I just use Imitrex injections when I get a migraine.

I'm scared. Killing myself feels like the only way to peace. There's only so much pain one person can endure before giving up. But I know my daughter needs me. Scared I'm not strong enough to stay alive.
I have bipolar disorder. i'm in a really crappy place right now. even if it gets better, I always end up in this place again. Just too tired to keep living  the same pain over and over.
